pos.personaBrief: Gasperini's Atalanta ranked mid-table in possession and played quick, risky, vertical transitions (Scouted), with a high man-to-man press to win the ball high (Il Post), so ball ownership is not the aim; chances created are.

pro.personaBrief: The team wants to make things happen quickly, take risks while the opponent is out of shape (Scouted), and defenders anticipate to restart fast (Il Post); build-up is secondary to speed.

est.personaBrief: A 3-4-2-1/3-4-3 with defined roles and wing-backs holding the flanks, but fluid mobile quadrilaterals near the ball and third players running into the box (Il Foglio); man-marking makes players leave zones.

lar.personaBrief: Width comes from the wing-backs, who stretch the defense and cross (Kompas, Il Post, The Analyst), with the two behind the striker as central goal threats; wide wingers per se are not the key.

blo.personaBrief: Aggressive man-to-man high press, forwards pressing from the start, immediate winning of the ball near the opponent's goal (Il Post, Scouted, Kompas, Il Foglio); it is not a low block.

mar.personaBrief: Individual marking all over the pitch is the signature, with centre-backs following their men across the pitch; Gasperini stayed loyal to it while others went zonal (Il Foglio, Chiesa di Totti, Corriere dello Sport).

pla.personaBrief: Gasperini kept the same man-marking model throughout his career (Chiesa di Totti), imposing it on new squads and players; he evolves with his players but not by opponent.

res.personaBrief: Gasperini says defense makes you invincible but to win you must attack; an attacking, risk-taking identity ('antithesis of Italian defensive football'), not a pragmatic result-first approach.

sis.personaBrief: A system of heavy duties and a collective that turns modest players into stars (Lookman transformed, cheap youngsters per Il Foglio, Corriere dello Sport); even creative players must track back and run.

jog.personaBrief: Athletic wing-backs covering the whole flank, running and duels in the man-marking press (Scouted, Il Post); Tudor says physicality cancels out quality and dropped Payet for lack of running.

bas.personaBrief: Gasperini develops young unknowns (Conti, Caldara, Gagliardini) and relies on smart buying and selling on a modest budget (Il Foglio, Corriere dello Sport); not a pure academy model.

lid.personaBrief: Gasperini admits to an iron-fist reputation, demands rules for all and presses duties on stars; Tudor dropped Payet and told players they did not run enough, though Gasperini says convincing the player works best.
